Blake Snell discusses pivotal seventh inning in Dodgers’ NLCS loss to Brewers
Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell described what led to his difficult seventh inning against Milwaukee in Game 3 of the NLCS. After dominating early innings and then surrendering key home runs late in his outing, Snell reflected on learning from mistakes as Los Angeles faces potential elimination.
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell discussed on Oct. 14 what went wrong during the crucial seventh inning that shifted momentum in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
Snell began his outing by surrendering a home run on his first pitch but then struck out nine batters over the next six innings, maintaining control until the seventh. After the Dodgers took their first lead of the night with a two-RBI double by Will Smith in the bottom of the sixth, Snell walked Andrew Vaughn to start the top of the seventh. Jake Bauers followed with an 11-pitch at-bat that ended in a two-run home run, and Garret Mitchell hit another homer immediately after, giving Milwaukee a 4-2 lead.
Snell was removed from the game following these events, and Milwaukee extended its advantage to secure a 3-0 series lead. The sudden shift raised questions among fans about Snell’s performance fluctuations during his start.
Afterward, Snell addressed reporters about giving up three home runs: “It’s pretty frustrating,” he said, adding that he had not given up any homers during his limited playing time this season. “It’s something I’ve got to learn from, it’s part of their journey too, and it’s only going to make me better in the long run,” he said from the clubhouse.
Regarding Bauers’ at-bat, Snell said: “Hats off to him. What an at-bat,” and continued: “I threw everything I had. Fastball down the middle, if I could locate that better, who knows what would have happened? This is the best I’ve ever seen him play. It’s a good at-bat. Hats off to him.”
Looking ahead as Los Angeles faces elimination and a possible sweep at Dodger Stadium on Thursday—now scheduled for 5 p.m., not 6 p.m.—Snell commented, “Yeah, it sucks, but it’s part of it. How do we bounce back, how do we fight? I think that’s the most important thing, us coming together and finding a way to win.”
